import numpy as np


def psi(reference, current, n_bins=10, eps=1e-4):
    """Population Stability Index with quantile bins fixed from `reference`.

    Out-of-range current values fall into the first/last bin. Bin
    proportions are floored at `eps` so an empty bin gives a large but
    finite term instead of log(0). NaN/inf are ignored (monitor the null
    rate separately); a constant or two-valued reference gets one bin per value.
    """
    ref = np.asarray(reference, dtype=float)
    cur = np.asarray(current, dtype=float)
    ref = ref[np.isfinite(ref)]
    cur = cur[np.isfinite(cur)]
    if ref.size == 0 or cur.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("reference and current need at least one finite value")
    edges = np.unique(np.quantile(ref, np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n_bins + 1)))
    inner = edges[1:-1]
    if inner.size == 0:
        # constant or two-valued reference: give each value its own bin plus
        # an open bin on each side, so any change is still visible
        inner = np.unique(np.concatenate([edges, np.nextafter(edges, np.inf)]))
    ref_idx = np.searchsorted(inner, ref, side="right")
    cur_idx = np.searchsorted(inner, cur, side="right")
    k = inner.size + 1
    p = np.bincount(ref_idx, minlength=k) / ref.size
    q = np.bincount(cur_idx, minlength=k) / cur.size
    p = np.maximum(p, eps)
    q = np.maximum(q, eps)
    return float(np.sum((q - p) * np.log(q / p)))

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
ref_big = rng.normal(0, 1, 20000)
same = rng.normal(0, 1, 20000)
assert psi(ref_big, same) < 0.01
assert psi(ref_big, ref_big) == 0.0
shifted = rng.normal(0.5, 1, 20000)
assert 0.15 < psi(ref_big, shifted) < 0.35
# empty bin: all current values above the reference's 90th percentile region
cur = np.full(1000, 5.0)
v_small = psi(ref_big, cur, eps=1e-6)
v_big = psi(ref_big, cur, eps=1e-2)
assert v_small > v_big > 0
# degenerate references: constant and binary features must still register a change
assert psi(np.zeros(100), np.zeros(100)) == 0.0
assert psi(np.zeros(100), np.full(100, 9.0)) > 5
binary = np.r_[np.zeros(50), np.ones(50)]
assert psi(binary, binary) == 0.0
assert psi(binary, np.ones(100)) > 1
# NaNs are ignored rather than silently counted in the top bin
nan_cur = np.r_[ref_big[:5000], np.full(50, np.nan)]
assert np.isfinite(psi(ref_big, nan_cur))
# small-sample instability: same distribution, 200 vs 200
def null_stats(bins, n=200, reps=300):
    r = np.random.default_rng(1)
    vals = [psi(r.normal(size=n), r.normal(size=n), n_bins=bins) for _ in range(reps)]
    return float(np.mean(vals)), float(np.std(vals))
m10, s10 = null_stats(10)
m40, s40 = null_stats(40)
assert m40 > 3 * m10
assert 0.05 < m10 < 0.15 and m40 > 0.25
print(round(psi(ref_big, shifted),3), v_small, v_big, m10, s10, m40, s40, 9*0.01, 39*0.01)

def _make_model(leak_weight):
    w = np.array([0.9, 1.1, 0.0, leak_weight])  # missed_payments, utilisation, customer_hash, postcode_hash
    def predict(X):
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-(X @ w - 0.2)))
    return predict


rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
X = np.column_stack([
    rng.integers(0, 6, 500).astype(float),   # missed_payments (col 0)
    rng.uniform(0, 1, 500),                  # utilisation (col 1)
    rng.uniform(0, 1, 500),                  # customer_hash (col 2)
    rng.uniform(0, 1, 500),                  # postcode_hash (col 3)
])
checks = {
    "hash_invariance": lambda p, A: invariance_failures(p, A, 2, lambda c: 1.0 - c, tol=0.01),
    "postcode_invariance": lambda p, A: invariance_failures(p, A, 3, lambda c: 1.0 - c, tol=0.01),
    "more_missed_not_safer": lambda p, A: directional_failures(p, A, 0, 1.0, direction=+1),
}
limits = {"hash_invariance": 0.0, "postcode_invariance": 0.0, "more_missed_not_safer": 0.0}

ok, rates = behavioural_report(_make_model(0.0), X, checks, limits)
assert ok and all(v == 0.0 for v in rates.values()), rates
# the missed-payments weight has the wrong sign here, so the directional check must trip
w_bad = np.array([-0.9, 1.1, 0.0, 0.0])
bad = lambda A: 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-(A @ w_bad)))
bad_ok, bad_rates = behavioural_report(bad, X, checks, limits)
assert not bad_ok and bad_rates["more_missed_not_safer"] == 1.0, bad_rates
# a model that leaks the postcode feature trips only the postcode invariance check
leaky_ok, leaky_rates = behavioural_report(_make_model(0.8), X, checks, limits)
assert not leaky_ok
assert leaky_rates["postcode_invariance"] > 0.5 and leaky_rates["hash_invariance"] == 0.0
# integer-typed feature matrices must not silently truncate the perturbation
Xi = np.column_stack([np.arange(6), np.arange(6)])
assert len(directional_failures(lambda A: A @ np.array([-1.0, 0.0]), Xi, 0, 0.5, direction=+1)) == 6
assert len(invariance_failures(lambda A: A @ np.array([1.0, 0.0]), Xi, 0, lambda c: c + 0.5, tol=0.1)) == 6
# float32 input stays float32 (no cast noise), and NaN scores are failures rather than silent passes
Xf = np.random.default_rng(0).uniform(size=(100, 2)).astype(np.float32)
f32 = lambda A: A @ np.array([0.5, 0.0], dtype=A.dtype)
assert len(directional_failures(f32, Xf, 0, 0.0)) == 0
nan_model = lambda A: np.where(A[:, 0] > 0.5, np.nan, A[:, 0])
n_nan = int((Xf[:, 0] > 0.5).sum())
assert n_nan > 0 and len(invariance_failures(nan_model, Xf, 1, lambda c: 1 - c)) == n_nan
assert len(directional_failures(nan_model, Xf, 1, 1.0)) == n_nan
print(rates, bad_rates, leaky_rates)

import sqlite3

SQL = """SELECT f.feature,
       COUNT(*) AS n_rows,
       SUM(CASE WHEN f.feature_ts > r.prediction_ts THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_from_future,
       ROUND(1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN f.feature_ts > r.prediction_ts THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS future_share,
       ROUND(MAX((julianday(f.feature_ts) - julianday(r.prediction_ts)) * 24), 1) AS max_hours_ahead,
       SUM(CASE WHEN f.feature_ts > r.label_ts THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_after_label
FROM training_rows AS r
JOIN training_features AS f ON f.row_id = r.row_id
GROUP BY f.feature
HAVING rows_from_future > 0
ORDER BY future_share DESC, f.feature;"""


def audit_leakage(conn):
    return conn.execute(SQL).fetchall()

import math


def daily_cost(hourly_rps, rps_per_replica, target_util, cost_per_replica_hour,
               min_replicas=2, cache_hit=0.0, static_replicas=None):
    """Return (cost, requests, cost_per_1k_requests) for one day.

    hourly_rps: 24 average request rates. A cache hit removes that share of requests from the model tier.
    static_replicas: if set, that many replicas run all day; otherwise replicas follow load each hour.
    """
    requests = sum(r * 3600 for r in hourly_rps)
    cost = 0.0
    for r in hourly_rps:
        model_rps = r * (1.0 - cache_hit)
        if static_replicas is not None:
            n = static_replicas
        else:
            n = max(min_replicas, math.ceil(model_rps / (rps_per_replica * target_util)))
        cost += n * cost_per_replica_hour
    return cost, requests, 1000.0 * cost / requests

import sqlite3

SQL = """
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00', s.served_at) AS hour,
       s.feature,
       COUNT(*) AS n,
       SUM(CASE WHEN r.request_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS not_recomputed,
       SUM(CASE WHEN r.request_id IS NOT NULL AND (
             (s.value IS NULL) <> (r.value IS NULL)
             OR ABS(s.value - r.value) > t.abs_tol + t.rel_tol * ABS(r.value)
           ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS mismatched
FROM served s
JOIN tolerances t ON t.feature = s.feature
LEFT JOIN recomputed r ON r.request_id = s.request_id AND r.feature = s.feature
GROUP BY hour, s.feature
HAVING mismatched > 0 OR not_recomputed > 0
ORDER BY hour, s.feature;
"""


def consistency_report(conn):
    return conn.execute(SQL).fetchall()

def _build():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    conn.executescript("""
    CREATE TABLE served (request_id TEXT, feature TEXT, value REAL, served_at TEXT);
    CREATE TABLE recomputed (request_id TEXT, feature TEXT, value REAL);
    CREATE TABLE tolerances (feature TEXT PRIMARY KEY, abs_tol REAL, rel_tol REAL);
    INSERT INTO tolerances VALUES ('orders_24h', 0.0, 0.0), ('avg_basket', 0.01, 0.001);
    """)
    rows_s, rows_r = [], []
    # 13:xx requests: served == recomputed (avg_basket differs by float noise only)
    for i in range(10):
        rid = "a%d" % i
        rows_s += [(rid, "orders_24h", float(i), "2026-03-01 13:%02d:00" % (i * 5)),
                   (rid, "avg_basket", 20.0 + i, "2026-03-01 13:%02d:00" % (i * 5))]
        rows_r += [(rid, "orders_24h", float(i)), (rid, "avg_basket", 20.0 + i + 0.004)]
    # 14:xx requests (after a hypothetical deploy): served orders_24h is off by 1 for 4 of 10
    for i in range(10):
        rid = "b%d" % i
        served_val = float(i + (1 if i < 4 else 0))
        rows_s += [(rid, "orders_24h", served_val, "2026-03-01 14:%02d:00" % (i * 5)),
                   (rid, "avg_basket", 20.0 + i, "2026-03-01 14:%02d:00" % (i * 5))]
        rows_r += [(rid, "orders_24h", float(i)), (rid, "avg_basket", 20.0 + i)]
    # one 14:xx request whose avg_basket was NULL when served but is 25.0 offline,
    # and one request that has no offline recomputation at all
    rows_s += [("c0", "avg_basket", None, "2026-03-01 14:50:00"),
               ("c1", "orders_24h", 3.0, "2026-03-01 14:55:00")]
    rows_r += [("c0", "avg_basket", 25.0)]
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO served VALUES (?,?,?,?)", rows_s)
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO recomputed VALUES (?,?,?)", rows_r)
    return conn


out = consistency_report(_build())
assert out == [("2026-03-01 14:00", "avg_basket", 11, 0, 1),
               ("2026-03-01 14:00", "orders_24h", 11, 1, 4)], out
print(out)
